items.headline: Markets Drifted on Friday, Closing a Jittery Week Lower Amid Tech Weakness and Geopolitical Concerns.
items.summary: U.S. equities saw a mixed close on Friday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average posted gains, while the S&P 500 edged higher, and the Nasdaq Composite fell. Concerns over elevated AI spending, rising oil prices due to Middle East tensions, and new tariffs weighed on investor sentiment, leading all three major indexes to finish the week lower.

items.headline: Digital Realty Soared on Upbeat Outlook.
items.summary: Shares of Digital Realty Trust ($DLR) jumped 15% and were on track for their best day since 2009 after the firm raised its full-year forecast for funds from operations.

items.headline: Tenet Healthcare Posted Significant Gains.
items.summary: Tenet Healthcare Corp. ($THC) saw its shares rise over 17%.

items.headline: Sandisk Corporation Tumbled Amid Broader Memory Stock Weakness.
items.summary: Sandisk Corporation dropped almost 11% alongside other memory stocks, reflecting continued tech weakness.

items.headline: Intel Fell Despite Strong Earnings Forecast.
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) shares declined 6.5% as investors focused on increased capital expenditure plans for AI despite the chipmaker forecasting quarterly profit and revenue above Wall Street estimates.

items.headline: SK Hynix Dragged Down by Semiconductor Weakness.
items.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix saw a significant decline of 7.9% as the semiconductor sector broadly struggled.

items.headline: Real Estate and Financials Led Gains; Technology Lagged.
items.summary: On Friday, the Real Estate sector rose 2.3% and led gains on the S&P 500, with Financial Services also performing strongly. Conversely, the Technology sector, particularly semiconductors, experienced significant declines due to concerns over AI spending. Communication Services and Consumer Discretionary sectors also faced selling pressure.

items.headline: Upcoming Fed Meeting and Geopolitical Risks in Focus.
items.summary: Investors are looking ahead to next week's Federal Reserve meeting for cues on interest rates, with the central bank widely expected to hold rates steady, though uncertainty persists with new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Escalating tensions in the Middle East continued to push oil prices higher, fanning inflation fears. Additionally, the Trump administration imposed new tariffs on goods from 60 trading partners, adding to trade policy uncertainty.

items.headline: AI Spending Concerns Weigh on Tech Earnings.
items.summary: The earnings season continued to highlight investor scrutiny over AI-related spending. Intel's shares fell despite an upbeat forecast as investors focused on capital expenditure plans. Earlier reports from Alphabet and Tesla also deepened concerns about rising capital spending and cash burn among major technology companies, setting a cautious tone for upcoming reports from Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta.
